pure_bond_tail_theorem.scope: This is an exact single-layer and telescope identity. It does not bound onsite history tails or prove convergence of the complete split product.

no_overclaim: This package proves the fifth-moment, elliptic, subset-shear, twentieth-history and hard-cutoff conclusions only for the registered fixed-beta finite periodic Q3 family with compact sources and the declared split histories. The v2.3 implementer estimate is a two-sided Gibbs Hilbert-Schmidt estimate for the split-product difference itself, not an arbitrary-observable conjugation estimate. The conditional connected-envelope theorem assumes maximum degree z, one uniform geometric coefficient envelope, and a separate uniform difference envelope for cutoff convergence. The second-order theorem concerns only the actual onsite-resolvent coefficient and requires parity-preserving cutoffs commuting with the onsite resolvent plus a source-uniform tail norm tau_M tending to zero; v2.1 Ritz monotonicity alone does not imply that hypothesis. The shear form estimate itself is uniform only for tested nearest-neighbor subsets on finite subgraphs or periodic quotients of Z^3, or under an explicitly uniform cubic-polynomial-growth hypothesis. A maximum-degree-six hypothesis alone is insufficient because bounded-degree graphs may have exponential growth. An arbitrary boundary family is not promoted to the actual history theorem without both this growth control and its own uniform static Gibbs input. This package does not prove n-to-infinity Trotter convergence, all-shape or all-exhaustion Cauchy compatibility, a surjective all-exhaustion common alpha, inverse or group/generator completion, a phase-KMS quotient, all-order connected rank-two unbounded block diagonalization, an all-order oscillator effective interaction or cutoff theorem, two-phase QPS for the exact oscillator lattice, beta-infinity phase identification, a broken-sector oscillator temporal mass or GNS gap, regulator removal, continuum, a same-Hamiltonian physical-empty comparison, a prospective blind validation result, C6, CP1, physical Sector A, or Pre-A closure. The UHF fixture rejects only automatic surjectivity and inverse-Cauchy inference from forward local stabilization; it is not a no-go for a Q3 common dynamics. The earlier rank-two fixture refutes only an automatic local-edge-to-global-gap inference; it is not a Q3 locality, local coercivity, or gap no-go.

full_hamiltonian_gibbs_resummation.two_orientation_bound: For U(t)=exp(-itH/hbar) and U_L(t)=exp(-itH_L/hbar), both ||(U-U_L)rho^(1/2)||_2 and ||rho^(1/2)(U-U_L)||_2 are at most |t| rho(W_L^2)^(1/2)/hbar. One opposite Duhamel ordering is used per orientation; rho commutes only with the full U.
full_hamiltonian_gibbs_resummation.state_stability: Because U rho U*=rho, ||rho-U_L rho U_L*||_1 is at most 2|t|rho(W_L^2)^(1/2)/hbar.
full_hamiltonian_gibbs_resummation.bounded_context_transfer: If A rho^(1/2)=rho^(1/2) C_A and A* rho^(1/2)=rho^(1/2) C_Astar with both half-modular contexts bounded, the two state-weighted automorphism seminorms transfer with factors ||A||+||C_A|| and ||A||+||C_Astar||. A sufficient narrow class is a finite Bohr-frequency decomposition A=sum A_omega, [H,A_omega]=omega A_omega, |omega|<=Omega, sum||A_omega||<infinity; then each half-modular context is bounded by exp(beta Omega/2) sum||A_omega||. Mere matrix bandwidth without this projective decomposition is not asserted.
full_hamiltonian_gibbs_resummation.scope: This is a finite-volume static-full-Gibbs unitary and state theorem. It does not pass arbitrary bounded contexts, control onsite-interspersed history states, prove a local automorphism limit, or close the common-alpha parent.
full_hamiltonian_gibbs_resummation.q3_form_domain_instantiation: For the registered finite-volume Q3 hard/form-cutoff pair, H and H_L are the closed form sums on the common quartic form domain; W_L is a real quadratic coordinate multiplier (possibly hard-tail restricted), W_L^2 has quartic growth, and the existing finite-volume Gibbs coordinate moments give rho(W_L^2)<infinity. Truncate W_L spectrally/formwise to bounded W_L,M, apply bounded Duhamel, then use form/strong-resolvent convergence and W_L,M rho^(1/2)->W_L rho^(1/2) in S2 to close the displayed bounds. This instantiation is for that hard/form pair; a differently defined smooth clipped-coordinate cutoff requires its own common-domain/form-convergence check.

conditional_fifth_graph_transport.C1_form_hypothesis: For the simultaneous all-cross-bond generator V_x and B_delta=exp(-i delta V_x/hbar), K_e^5 has an invariant form domain, the quadratic-form derivative is <B_delta psi,(i/hbar)[V_x,K_e^5]B_delta psi>, and G5=sup ||K_e^(-5/2)(i/hbar)[V_x,K_e^5]K_e^(-5/2)|| is finite uniformly in all declared indices.
conditional_fifth_graph_transport.commutator_expansion: With J_e=(i/hbar)[V_x,K_e], G5 is bounded by ||K_e^(-1/2)J_eK_e^(-1/2)||+2||K_e^(1/2)J_eK_e^(-3/2)||+2||K_e^(3/2)J_eK_e^(-5/2)||. The exact grouped coefficients are 1,2,2.
conditional_fifth_graph_transport.transport: The graph norm obeys ||K_e^(5/2)B_delta K_e^(-5/2)||<=exp(G5|delta|/2). Onsite product steps commute with K_e; bond steps of total absolute time at most T therefore give each orientation a K_e^5 moment at most exp(G5 T) S_mu^5 m5.
conditional_fifth_graph_transport.sharp_result: Strong commutativity gives phi(K_e^5)<=S_mu^5 m5, while X_e^20<=|q_x|^20+|q_y|^20<=d5^2(k_x^5+k_y^5)<=d5^2K_e^5. Hence M20<=2 d5^2 exp(G5 T) S_mu^5 m5.
conditional_fifth_graph_transport.scope: This v2.1 implication is retained. R-167 v2.2 discharges its m5, d5 and fifth-graph inputs in the registered fixed-beta periodic compact-source scope; it is not an all-exhaustion or thermodynamic automorphism theorem.

all_order_graph_growth_no_go.fixture: For K=diag(1,4), V=sigma_x and hbar=1, C_m=K^(-m/2)i[V,K^m]K^(-m/2) has exact norm 2^m-2^(-m). For A_m(t)=K^(m/2)exp(-itV)K^(-m/2), A_m(t)^*A_m(t)=I+tC_m+O(t^2), and the right Dini derivative of log||A_m(t)||, equivalently t down to zero after maximizing over plus/minus t, is ||C_m||/2.
all_order_graph_growth_no_go.consequence: Any bound ||A_m(t)||<=exp(G_m|t|/2) forces G_m>=2^m-2^(-m). Therefore low-order graph information does not automatically give a quadratic-in-m all-order hierarchy.
all_order_graph_growth_no_go.scope: This abstract normalized-commutator fixture rejects only an automatic all-m inference. A Q3 embedding would additionally require a proved nonzero onsite spectral transition. It does not reject existence of the fixed m=5 constant G5.

static_moment_low_graph_no_go.fixture: Let K_N=diag(1,N^4), q_N=diag(0,N), H_N=diag(0,N^4), rho_N proportional to exp(-H_N), V_N=sigma_y/N^4 and U_N(delta)=exp(-i delta V_N), with delta nonzero and N^4>=|delta|. Then d5=1 and rho_N(K_N^5)<=1+(5/e)^5. For every 0<=s<=1, ||K_N^s U_N(delta)K_N^(-s)||<=1+|delta|, yet the exact fifth normalized commutator constant is G5=N^6-N^(-14).
static_moment_low_graph_no_go.history_tail: Using sin(x)^2>=x^2/4 for |x|<=1 and the ground Gibbs weight at least one half, each of the plus/minus history orientations has q_N^20 moment at least delta^2 N^12/8, so their sum is at least delta^2 N^12/4.
static_moment_low_graph_no_go.scope: This rejects automatic promotion from static moments plus graph control only through 0<=s<=1 to a uniform twentieth history moment. It is not a Q3 dynamics no-go and is consistent with the conditional theorem once the growing G5 is retained.

full_oscillator_edge_cluster.setup: For z=6 set h_xy=[(h_x-epsilon0)+(h_y-epsilon0)]/z+B_xy with B_xy=(c/2)sum_e(q_xe-q_ye)^2. Let P be the onsite even/odd doublet, P0 the aligned s-spin span, L the low misaligned span and Q=1-P_xP_y. Put Cb=8c(a0-m^2), fb=delta1/z+4cd2, eb=Cb+fb, J=8cm^2, epsilon=8c(b+2ma+a^2), A=eb+2J and D=Gamma/z.
full_oscillator_edge_cluster.compressions: The exact diagonal compressions are P0 h_xy P0=eb P0 and L h_xy L=(eb+2J)L; Q h_xy Q>=D Q and ||Q h_xy P_xP_y||<=epsilon. Generally P0 h_xy L is nonzero and has norm |fb|, so no block-diagonal or invariant-subspace statement is made.
full_oscillator_edge_cluster.sharp_minmax: If h_xy commutes with global parity, is nonnegative with compact resolvent, eb>=0, J>0, D>eb and epsilon^2<2J(D-eb), define gb=(A+D-sqrt((D-A)^2+4epsilon^2))/2. Then gb>eb; there is exactly one even and one odd eigenvalue at most eb, lambda3>=gb, and lambda3-lambda2>=gb-eb. When D>A, gb-eb>=2J-epsilon^2/(D-A).
full_oscillator_edge_cluster.relative_form: With k=h_site-epsilon0-delta1P1, h0=(k_x+k_y)/z+J(1-s_xs_y), gamma0=min(Gamma/z,2J), rho_b=eta_b+nu_b/Gamma and ell_b=8c(a0-m^2)+8c|d2|, for tau>0 the remainder obeys |<V>|<=alpha<h0>+beta||.||^2 with alpha=z[rho_b+J/Gamma+epsilon^2/(tau Gamma)] and beta=2delta1/z+ell_b+tau. If alpha<1 and Delta_rf=(1-alpha)gamma0-2beta>0, the same parity count holds and lambda3-lambda2>=Delta_rf.
full_oscillator_edge_cluster.spectral_cutoff_removal: For nested parity-preserving onsite spectral projections Pi_M>=P whose union is a quartic form core, restrict the original full form by Pi_M tensor Pi_M. The same constants hold and the Ritz eigenvalues decrease to the full edge eigenvalues, preserving the uniform lower gap. Replacing q by Pi_M q Pi_M before squaring is not this construction because Pi_M q^2 Pi_M need not equal (Pi_M q Pi_M)^2.
full_oscillator_edge_cluster.asymptotic_scope: In the v1.9 N corridor, eb=O(N^-6), epsilon=O(N^-3), D is asymptotic to a positive constant times N^2 and 2J tends to 16, so the sharp local edge gap tends to 16 with O(N^-8) mixing correction. The relative-form alpha=O(N^-2) and beta=O(N^-3). This is local edge coercivity only, not a linked-cluster elimination, oscillator QPS theorem, or oscillator-lattice GNS gap.

actual_q3_static_fifth_moment_and_ellipt.scope: Registered finite periodic Q3 volumes at fixed beta, uniformly over sites/translates and the registered compact source set. No arbitrary-boundary extension is asserted.
actual_q3_static_fifth_moment_and_ellipt.virial_identity: For A_i=(q_i p_i^9+p_i^9 q_i)/2 and F_i=partial_i V, on the Schwartz core (i/hbar)[H,A_i]=p_i^10/chi-(1/2)sum_(j=0)^8[q_i p_i^j F_i p_i^(8-j)+p_i^j F_i p_i^(8-j) q_i].
actual_q3_static_fifth_moment_and_ellipt.critical_bound: The fixed-star degree-at-most-three force and anisotropic normal-order/Young estimate bound the complete force sum by 9 epsilon <p_i^10>+C_epsilon<1+Q_star^20>. Choose 9 epsilon<1/chi. Polynomially confining finite-volume eigenvectors are Schwartz; sum only through a finite spectral cutoff, then pass monotonically using the registered periodic compact-source coordinate exponential estimate. No unbounded trace cyclicity is used.
actual_q3_static_fifth_moment_and_ellipt.elliptic_embedding: Uniformly on the compact onsite-source set, the quartic Shubin graph induction for m<=5 equates the k_h^(m/2) graph norm with monomials |beta|+|alpha|/2<=m. Hence k_h^5<=C(1+sum_i p_i^10+|q|^20) as forms and || |q|^10 k_h^(-5/2)||<=C.
actual_q3_static_fifth_moment_and_ellipt.conclusion: m5<infinity and d5<infinity uniformly in the declared scope.

direct_subset_shear_fifth_graph_propagat.setup: For f_x=exp(-mu d(x,e)), K_e=sum_x f_x k_x, a tested nearest-neighbor bond subset F of a finite subgraph or periodic quotient of Z^3, V_F=-c sum_(xy in F)q_x dot q_y, and B_F(delta)=exp(-i delta V_F/hbar), put Q_x^F=sum_(y:xy in F)q_y.
direct_subset_shear_fifth_graph_propagat.exact_conjugation: On Schwartz, B_F(delta)^*K_eB_F(delta)=K_e+delta R1+delta^2 R2, R1=(c/chi)sum_x f_x p_x dot Q_x^F and R2=(c^2/(2chi))sum_x f_x|Q_x^F|^2.
direct_subset_shear_fifth_graph_propagat.fifth_form_bound: Finite noncommutative expansion and the tensorized m=5 graph estimate use ord(k)=1, ord(p)=1/2 and ord(q)=1/4. For an R1 monomial f_x p_x q_y, pay f_x^(1/2) to p_x and f_y^(1/4) to q_y; neighbor comparability leaves at most exp(mu/4) f_x^(1/4). Expand an R2 anchor as f_x|Q_x^F|^2=f_x sum_(y,z~x)q_y dot q_z. For each cross monomial pay f_y^(1/4)f_z^(1/4), leaving at most exp(mu/2) f_x^(1/2). The K_e^5 multinomial supplies these allocated weights; commutators are lower order and K_e>=1 fills slack. On finite cubic subgraphs and periodic quotients, sum_x f_x^(1/4)<=2[(1+exp(-mu/4))/(1-exp(-mu/4))]^3. At most five nonbaseline anchors occur. If n1 are R1 and n2 are R2, their neighbor-incidence count is n1+2n2<=10, so the unreduced safe tuple count is at most 6^10; no diagonal-only reduction of R2 is assumed. Thus for |delta|<=T, |<psi,(B^*K_e^5B-K_e^5)psi>|<=C5(T,mu)|delta|<psi,K_e^5psi>. Every nonbaseline word contains delta; this O(|delta|) factor is load-bearing.
direct_subset_shear_fifth_graph_propagat.domain_and_transport: The plus/minus-delta estimates give onto invariance of D(K_e^(5/2)) and ||K_e^(5/2)B_F(delta)K_e^(-5/2)||<=exp(C5|delta|/2). The form-C1 constant obeys G5<=C5. Products of arbitrary partial or reverse tested nearest-neighbor subsets within the declared cubic graph with sum_j|delta_j|<=T are uniform; onsite factors commute with K_e.
direct_subset_shear_fifth_graph_propagat.uniformity_boundary: The direct shear bound is uniform in finite cubic volume, tested edge, tested nearest-neighbor subset, periodic quotient or finite subgraph, and compact onsite source. The same proof applies to a declared graph family only if it carries a uniform cubic-polynomial-growth bound. Maximum degree at most six alone is not enough. Combination with the static Gibbs input is made only for the registered periodic compact-source family.
direct_subset_shear_fifth_graph_propagat.generic_degree_six_hostile: A six-regular tree has sphere sizes 6*5^(r-1). At exp(-mu/4)=1/2 the weighted sphere terms grow as 3*(5/2)^(r-1), so the residual sum diverges. This rejects promotion from cubic volumes to arbitrary degree-six graphs.

actual_q3_twentieth_history_and_hard_cut.scope: Registered fixed-beta finite periodic Q3 volumes, compact sources, tested edge translates/orientations, partial and reverse split histories of total absolute time at most T.
actual_q3_twentieth_history_and_hard_cut.moment: M20<=2 d5^2 exp(C5 T) S_mu^5 m5.
actual_q3_twentieth_history_and_hard_cut.hard_cutoff: At L=R^(2/5), the two-orientation hard restricted-tail corridor is at most 2916 c^2 M20 R^(-2/5). The bounded-cutoff factorial logarithm is -R log(R)/5+O(R).
actual_q3_twentieth_history_and_hard_cut.boundary: This is not n-to-infinity/all-shape Cauchy convergence, an all-exhaustion common alpha, group/generator completion, or a KMS quotient.

rank_two_projection_gap_no_go.fixture: On onsite C^2 let n=|1><1|, phi^-=(|10>-|01>)/sqrt(2), and h_xy=|phi^-><phi^-|+n_x n_y. The local rank-two projection has spectrum {0,0,1,1} and one even plus one odd kernel vector. For every finite connected G, ker sum h_xy=span{vacuum,W_G}; on the one-particle sector the Hamiltonian is (1/2)L_G. On a d-torus its gap is at most 1-cos(2pi/L)<=2pi^2/L^2.
rank_two_projection_gap_no_go.infinite_onsite_lift: On ell^2(N_0), add K=z sum_(r>=2)(r-1)|r><r| and distribute (K_x+K_y)/z over edges. Each lifted edge retains the rank-two kernel and local gap one, while the same gapless one-particle band survives.
rank_two_projection_gap_no_go.scope: This refutes only the automatic inference from a local parity doublet and local edge gap to a volume-uniform lattice gap. It is not a no-go for Q3 locality, Q3 local coercivity, or a future Q3 gap theorem.

requirements: A parity-equivariant, boundary/source-uniform quasi-local U_Lambda and an effective low/high decomposition with a uniform high-sector gap.
A connected interaction Phi_eff with sup_x sum_(X contains x)|X| exp(a diam X)||Phi_eff(X)||<epsilon_QPS J.
Spectral-cutoff convergence in the same connected interaction norm.
A phasewise GNS intertwiner identifying the oscillator phases and their gap with the effective two-phase system.

registered_periodic_split_implementer_tw.scope: Registered fixed-beta finite periodic Q3 volumes with compact sources, every declared finite split mesh, every declared partial and reverse history, and total absolute bond time at most T.
registered_periodic_split_implementer_tw.seminorm: For a split-implementer difference X=P-P_L define ||X||_(rho,#1)=||X rho^(1/2)||_2+||rho^(1/2)X||_2.
registered_periodic_split_implementer_tw.opposite_telescopes: Use the Duhamel ordering opposite to the Gibbs weight on each Hilbert-Schmidt leg. If C_plus and C_minus are the v2.2 forward/reverse hard-tail bounds, then ||P-P_L||_(rho,#1)<=(T/hbar)(sqrt(C_plus)+sqrt(C_minus))<=(T/hbar)sqrt(2(C_plus+C_minus)).
registered_periodic_split_implementer_tw.paired_sum_input: The v2.2 registered-periodic authority gives C_plus+C_minus<=2916 c^2 M20 R^6 L^(-16). Therefore at L=R^(2/5), ||P-P_L||_(rho,#1)<=54 sqrt(2) |c| T sqrt(M20) hbar^(-1) R^(-1/5).
registered_periodic_split_implementer_tw.boundary: This is a mesh-uniform implementer estimate in a two-sided Gibbs Hilbert-Schmidt seminorm. It inserts no arbitrary bounded observable between the weighted legs and proves no surjective thermodynamic automorphism, inverse convergence, group, generator, or KMS quotient.

conditional_connected_cluster_geometric_.hypotheses: On a graph of maximum degree z with a fixed neighbor order, let Phi(X) vanish unless X is finite and connected and obey ||Phi(X)||<=A kappa^|X|. Choose a>0 with r=z^2 exp(a) kappa<1.
conditional_connected_cluster_geometric_.counting: A canonical rooted spanning tree followed by its deterministic depth-first traversal injects every connected n-set containing x into a walk of length 2(n-1), so their number is at most z^(2(n-1)); also diam(X)<=n-1.
conditional_connected_cluster_geometric_.qps_bound: sup_x sum_(X contains x)|X| exp(a diam(X))||Phi(X)||<=A kappa sum_(n>=1)n r^(n-1)=A kappa/(1-r)^2.
conditional_connected_cluster_geometric_.cutoff: If, separately, ||Phi_M(X)-Phi(X)||<=A_M kappa^|X| uniformly over the declared boundary/source/translate family and A_M tends to zero, then ||Phi_M-Phi||_a<=A_M kappa/(1-r)^2 tends to zero. Pointwise coefficient convergence without this uniform difference envelope is insufficient.
conditional_connected_cluster_geometric_.boundary: This is a conditional deterministic conversion theorem. It does not construct the all-order Q3 effective interaction or prove that its coefficients satisfy either envelope.

second_order_connected_onsite_resolvent_.setup: Let P be the product low-band projection, Q=1-P, K=sum_x k_x with K>=Gamma Q, and T_e=Q B_e P with ||T_e||<=epsilon. The actual second-order coefficient is Psi^(2)=-sum_(e,f) T_e^*(QKQ)^(-1)T_f.
second_order_connected_onsite_resolvent_.connectedness: K preserves exact onsite high-support sectors. Hence the ordered coefficient for disjoint e and f vanishes. For fixed x there are at most z diagonal pairs e=f containing x and at most 3z(z-1) ordered off-diagonal overlapping pairs whose union contains x.
second_order_connected_onsite_resolvent_.qps_bound: Every pair coefficient has norm at most epsilon^2/Gamma. Diagonal unions have |X|=2 and diam(X)<=1; off-diagonal unions have |X|<=3 and diam(X)<=2. Thus ||Psi^(2)||_a<=[2z exp(a)+9z(z-1)exp(2a)]epsilon^2/Gamma. In the v2.1 N corridor epsilon=O(N^-3) and Gamma is of order N^2, so this is O(N^-8)=o(J).
second_order_connected_onsite_resolvent_.ritz_cutoff: Let Pi_M be parity-preserving local Ritz/form projections which contain P and commute with the onsite resolvent. Put D_e=(QKQ)^(-1/2)T_e and D_e,M=(QKQ)^(-1/2)Pi_M T_e. If tau_M=sup_e||(1-Pi_M)T_e|| tends uniformly to zero over the registered compact source family, then ||D_e-D_e,M||<=tau_M/sqrt(Gamma), and the same QPS sum gives ||Psi_M^(2)-Psi^(2)||_a<=2 C_a epsilon tau_M/Gamma with C_a=2z exp(a)+9z(z-1)exp(2a).
second_order_connected_onsite_resolvent_.boundary: The uniform tail hypothesis is additional to v2.1 Ritz eigenvalue monotonicity. This second-order coefficient does not supply an all-order Lie-Schwinger/Feshbach expansion, its convergence radius, a phase intertwiner, or a broken-sector oscillator GNS gap.

forward_local_automorphism_limit_no_go.fixture: On the one-sided UHF algebra tensor_(j>=1) M_2, let alpha_N cyclically send sites 1,...,N to 2,...,N,1 and fix all later sites. For every local A, alpha_N(A) stabilizes exactly for large N to the unilateral right shift sigma(A)=1 tensor A.
forward_local_automorphism_limit_no_go.failure: The range of sigma has identity in the first tensor factor, so sigma is a proper endomorphism and Z_1 is not in its range. Moreover alpha_N^(-1)(Z_1)=Z_N and ||Z_N-Z_M||=2 for N!=M, so the inverses are not point-norm Cauchy.
forward_local_automorphism_limit_no_go.scope: This rejects only the inference from exact forward local stabilization of automorphisms to automatic surjectivity and inverse convergence. It does not reject a Q3 common alpha proved with independent inverse or group control.
